turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi. Well, I came in because I just can’t seem to stop launching projects. It's like... I start all these new work plans, or I'm making schedules for new IT certifications, upgrading the entire home network, even sending out messages to old contacts. 

It just gets so intense that I blow past normal limits. I just keep going and going until my wife, or my director at work, has to step in and tell me to stop.

symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes excessively launching multiple new work, technical, and social projects to an intense degree where they cannot stop until others intervene.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?
turns.patient_response:
Not really, no. I wouldn't say I act without thinking things through. 

If anything, I'm thinking about the details of these projects constantly. It's not like I'm just doing random, reckless things on a whim... I just take on way too many planned things at once and can't seem to put the brakes on. But I haven't noticed myself doing things impulsively without a plan, no.

symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes taking on far too many planned projects at once and being unable to slow down, indicating increased goal-directed activity.
symptom_reasoning.S041: The patient explicitly denies acting on impulse, without a plan, or engaging in reckless behaviors on a whim.

turns.doctor_question: Are these projects and activities causing problems in your relationships or daily life?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, they are. Um, at work, I was actually put on leave recently because a big server migration I was pushing for failed. I just pushed too hard, too fast. And at home, it's... it's definitely causing friction. My wife has had to step in a lot, mostly because of how much I'm spending on network gear, or because I'm up working half the night. We end up arguing a lot when we try to talk about it. 

And, honestly, I've just dropped out of everything else. I used to play music at church, go rock climbing, and I mentored some junior IT guys... but I've pulled away from all of that. I just can't seem to reliably show up or follow through on any of it right now.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel distressed or upset by your inability to stop launching these projects and activities?
turns.patient_response:
Honestly, no. I don't really feel upset by it. When I'm in the middle of planning everything out, it actually feels... well, it feels good. Like I'm getting ahead and doing important work. 

The only thing that bothers me is the fallout, you know? Like getting put on leave or the arguments at home. But the actual drive to keep starting things? No, that doesn't distress me at all.

turns.doctor_question: Have you always been like this, or is this something that has developed over time?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't always been like this. It's been going on for, I'd say, about two years and five months. It started right around the time I took on a major system migration role at work. That's when things really shifted.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often feel unusually happy or euphoric when you're working on these projects?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. Some weeks I feel almost electric, like I'm completely unstoppable. But it's not always just a happy feeling. It can turn pretty fast. If there's even a tiny delay, or... or if my wife just asks a simple question about what I'm working on, I can snap. It just feels like everyone is trying to slow me down on purpose, and that gets me really irritated.

symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient describes distinct periods of feeling 'electric' and 'unstoppable' that rapidly shift to snapping and becoming easily irritated over minor interruptions, indicating elevated and irritable mood with mood lability.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself feeling restless or having an inability to sit still when you're not working on one of your projects?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, definitely. I can't just sit down and relax anymore. If I'm not actively working on something, I... I end up pacing around the house, usually carrying my laptop with me. Or I'll suddenly decide I need to reorganize the entire garage, or I'll spend hours rewriting all my project boards. If I try to just sit on the couch and watch a show with my wife, I actually feel physically uncomfortable. It's like my body just won't let me stay still.

symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient describes persistent inability to sit still, pacing with a laptop, reorganizing the garage, and spending hours rewriting project boards due to physical discomfort when attempting to relax.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever experienced a period of time where you didn't need much sleep, yet you still felt rested and had a lot of energy?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, definitely. There have been these... these runs where I only sleep maybe three hours a night. I'll just wake up wide awake, sharp, right at 3 or 4 a.m. And I don't feel tired at all. It honestly just feels like I've been handed bonus time to get more things done.

symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient explicitly confirms having episodes where they only sleep about three hours a night and wake up feeling sharp and not tired at all, representing a decreased need for sleep.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely high or irritable that lasted for several days or more?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, they definitely last for several days at a time, sometimes longer. Um, I'd say these stretches—where I'm unusually driven, running on low sleep, and feeling really overconfident—they've been happening for a while now. It's been a part of my life for roughly a year and eight months.

symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient confirms having multi-day periods of feeling extremely high or irritable in direct response to the clinician's question.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient describes these stretches as being 'unusually driven,' indicating abnormally increased energy and goal-directed activity.
symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient reports feeling 'really overconfident' during these episodes, reflecting inflated self-esteem.
symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient notes that they are 'running on low sleep' during these periods, consistent with a decreased need for sleep.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever been hospitalized due to your behavior or symptoms related to these projects and activities?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't. I mean, my wife gets frustrated with me sometimes when I'm like this, but it's never gotten to the point where I had to go to a hospital or anything like that. I've always just stayed at home and kept working.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever experienced any break from reality, such as hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there, during these periods of high energy and activity?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, actually, I have. Um... during my most driven stretches, when I was barely sleeping and trying to push through these huge plans, I've had things like that happen. Like, I would hear actual comments coming from the server noise at work. Just voices mixed into the hum of the machines. And I was also reading these... hidden threats into my regular work messages and emails. So, yeah, that was all happening at the same time.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient reports reading hidden threats into ordinary work messages and emails, reflecting persecutory or referential delusions.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient confirms experiencing auditory hallucinations, specifically hearing voices and comments embedded in the sound of office servers.

top_partial.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever experienced any severe psychotic symptoms, such as delusions, during these periods of high energy and activity?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I have. But honestly, it's not just when I'm running on high energy. Even when my mood is totally normal, I get these... well, I get convinced about things. Like, I'll see a calendar invite or notice someone's Teams status change, or just hear a passing comment in the hallway, and I'm absolutely certain they're coded warnings. I get this strong belief that people are quietly building a case to push me out of the company. It feels very real, regardless of whether I'm in one of those energetic phases or not.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient describes persecutory and referential delusions, being convinced that everyday occurrences like Teams statuses and calendar invites are coded warnings that coworkers are plotting to push them out.
